# opencode-readseek

OpenCode plugin for anchored edits, structural search, symbol navigation, and
document inspection.

## Install

For OpenCode with the legacy server plugin API, add the plugin to `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["opencode-readseek"]
}
```

For OpenCode V2, install the package locally:

```sh
npm install --save-dev opencode-readseek
```

Then select the isolated entrypoint in your project's `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "plugins": ["./node_modules/opencode-readseek/dist/v2.js"]
}
```

Local plugin modules can also import the default export from `opencode-readseek/v2`.
This entrypoint does not load the legacy tool implementation. The existing
`opencode-readseek` and `opencode-readseek/server` entrypoints remain unchanged.

The V2 entrypoint supplies a ReadSeek skill and agent guidance only; it does not
register custom tools. The `readseek_*` tools listed below require the legacy
server plugin API. To use the V2 skill, install `@jarkkojs/readseek` globally so
`readseek` is on PATH; otherwise use OpenCode's built-in tools.

The plugin uses the AppImage on Linux and native executables on
macOS/Windows supplied by `@jarkkojs/readseek`. Set
`READSEEK_BINARY` to an absolute executable path to override it.

## Tools

- Read without inference: `readseek_show`, `readseek_tree`,
  `readseek_meta`, `readseek_assets`.
- Check: `readseek_syntax`, `readseek_check`.
- Explicit inference: `readseek_caption`, `readseek_objects`,
  `readseek_ocr`.
- Find: `readseek_grep`, `readseek_search`, `readseek_def`,
  `readseek_refs`.
- Mutate: `readseek_edit`, `readseek_rename`, `readseek_write`.

Tool names mirror native flat single-word commands, such as `show`,
`search`, and `edit`. Paths resolve against the project directory.
Use `at` selectors (`line:N[:COLUMN]`, `hash:H[:COLUMN]`, `symbol:NAME`,
`page:N`, `node:ID`, or `asset:ID`) where supported. Structure defaults to
`depth: 1`. Use separate structure, metadata, and syntax tools rather than
combining facets in a content request.

The four `show` tools return readable summaries and grouped text: anchored source
lines, document sections, structure trees, metadata fields, and asset paths.
Notices identify omitted ranges and how to continue. The unchanged native result
is retained separately in `metadata.readseek`; image attachments are unchanged.

`readseek_search` accepts `pattern`, `context` with `selector`, or `rule`.
`readseek_refs` requires exactly one of `name` or `at`; binding
references and renames use line or hash cursors. KDL selection/check rules
may be inline or `@path`; tool calls cannot supply standard input.

`readseek_grep` requires `pattern`: native UTF-8 RE2 regex by default, or exact
text with `literal: true`. Lookaround and backreferences are unsupported.
Native ReadSeek handles `ignoreCase`, `glob`, `context`, `summary`, and
`scope: "symbol"` grouping. `scopeContext` requires symbol scope. The positive
`limit` defaults to 100 matching lines, not occurrences. `gitScope` accepts
`tracked`, `untracked`, `ignored`, or `all` (default: tracked plus untracked).
Source hits carry editable `LINE:HASH` anchors; document hits carry node/page
selectors and do not mark files as editable.

Read fresh `LINE:HASH` anchors before editing. Each edit item contains exactly
one nested `set_line`, `replace_lines`, `insert_after`, `replace_symbol`, or
`replace` object. Edits and renames default to applying after a verified plan
and edit permission; use `apply: false` to preview and `planHash` to require
that plan when applying. `write` replaces complete text files.

Syntax and rule checks treat exit 1 as findings, not transport failure;
exit 0 is clean and exit 2 is failure. Syntax checks do not typecheck.

Assets auto-materialize into the cache. Content and asset tools return usable
cached paths and attach images according to `imageMode`; there is no extract
command or asset output-path parameter. Inference is only requested through
the explicit inference tools (`level: low|medium|high`, default `low`). Caption
`include` may request `text` and/or `objects`. Models must already be installed;
reading never silently invokes OCR or downloads a model.

To control image handling:

```json
{
  "plugin": [["opencode-readseek", { "imageMode": "auto" }]]
}
```

`imageMode` is `auto` (default), `on`, or `off`.

## Development

```sh
bun test
npm run build
npm run typecheck
```


For real-binary checks, set `READSEEK_BINARY` to the built native executable,
for example `/absolute/path/to/packages/readseek/build/readseek`.
